title: Preparing a rabbit for showing
subtitle: Grooming, condition, and ring presentation basics.
excerpt: Showing rabbits tests whether your animals match the British Rabbit Council breed standard in type, size, coat, and condition. Preparation starts weeks before the show date, and on the day most of it is grooming and presentation. A well-prepared rabbit needs to be clean, calm, and comfortable being handled by strangers.
sourceNotes: British Rabbit Council, Show Standards (2022 edn.). Meg Brown and Virginia Richardson, Rabbit Lopaedia (2000), showing chapter. British Rabbit Council, Guide to Preparing Your Rabbit for Exhibition (2021).

glossaryTerms.definition: The British Rabbit Council's written description of the ideal specimen of a breed, used by judges to score and place animals.
Training a rabbit to sit in the correct position on a show table so the judge can assess type and conformation.

content.text: Rabbit showing is organised through the British Rabbit Council (BRC) and affiliated breed clubs. Rabbits are judged against the
for their breed, covering type (body shape), coat, colour, size, and condition. The preparation window is 4 to 6 weeks before the show date.
Condition and coat 4 to 6 weeks out
Check the animal is in full coat and not moulting. A moult disqualifies or heavily penalises even a good specimen. Know your breed's moulting pattern and plan entries accordingly.
Confirm body condition: ribs just perceptible under a hand pressed lightly, no bony spine, no visible hip bones. A rabbit that is too thin or too fat will not make the right type in the ring.
Treat for any parasites well in advance. Ear mites, fur mites, or flystrike at the show are immediate grounds for removal.

is the skill of getting the rabbit to sit quietly on a show table in the position that shows its type to best advantage. Start by handling the rabbit on a flat table for 10 minutes per day. Gently encourage it into the correct pose for its breed (upright and composed for normal breeds; long and stretched for fur breeds). Reward stillness by leaving the rabbit undisturbed, not with food rewards.
Grooming in the week before the show

Remove all loose fur with a rubber grooming glove or a fine-toothed comb. Work with the lay of the coat, then against it to remove undercoat. Do not strip the coat on long-coated breeds within 2 weeks of the show.
Clean ears with a cotton ball dampened with a little warm water. Do not probe deep into the ear canal.
Trim nails to a short, neat length. Overgrown nails on a show rabbit are penalised, and long nails catch on pen wire and break.

On show day, a final polish of the coat with a chamois leather or velvet cloth brings up a natural sheen without leaving product residue. Do not use chalk, hairspray, or any coat preparations; these are prohibited in BRC shows.

Pens at BRC shows are small wire cages. Bring clean hay, a small water bottle, and a wooden board or show mat the rabbit already knows, so the pen feels familiar. Minimise handling by others before judging, but acclimatise the rabbit to the hall noise and movement before it goes into the pen.

attrs.cue: Rabbit goes into a full moult 2 weeks before the show
attrs.cause: Change in day length or an interruption in routine (moving pens, change of feed)
attrs.fix: Withdraw the entry. A moulting rabbit cannot be presented competitively. Re-enter for a show 8 to 10 weeks ahead when the new coat will have fully grown through.

attrs.cue: Rabbit flips and stamps during posing practice
attrs.cause: Not yet habituated to being placed on a raised flat surface, or over-handled
attrs.fix: Reduce daily sessions to 5 minutes. Place the rabbit on a surface close to the ground first, then raise to table height as confidence builds. Never restrain a rabbit that is panicking; put it down and try again later.
